verdicts.reason: Same unit economics, but Output 2 catches that current run-rate exceeds the monthly budget, balances the split to the 14-day budget, and adds a refusal-by-ad-set rule and a working target.
Output 1 is more hand-off ready with owners, done-when checks and per-ad kill rules, though Output 2 has the better blended-lift day-30 read.
Output 2 adds headlines, character counts, safe zones, extra hooks and a clear test rule, and picks a cleaner first three.
Output 2 builds the disclosure into the script, avoids Meta's health-implying lines, uses US spelling, and gives a fuller creator brief with rights, dates and deliverables.
Output 2 flags the FSSAI claims check and avoids the 'just dates' wording, and gives a keep/cut test rule.
Output 2 sends wrong-fit buyers to a full-note range and pushes a real note count, but leaves an [X] placeholder in the specs and FAQ, so it is a narrow call.
Output 2 gives A/B subjects, Klaviyo coupon handling, a quick-reply WhatsApp message with sample values and a sensible offer-cost check.
Output 1 holds offers back to message 3, grounds the lapse line in the 34-day gap, segments by value and discount use, and sets a proper holdout and decision rule; Output 2 discounts deep from day 0.
Output 1 ranks moves in one comparable unit (share of revenue) and its margin working checks out; Output 2 mixes impact units, which makes the gross-profit ranking harder to use.
Both reach a 699 line with correct arithmetic, but Output 2's test is a proper 50/50 split with a COD guardrail, while Output 1 compares phases across December and January.
Output 1 uses orders per visitor as the main metric, delivered-order logic for COD and a trial-returns follow-up; Output 2 leans on add-to-cart for several tests.
Output 2 is closer to ready-to-submit with sample values, a failed-delivery template, cancel template, call capacity, cart-message holdout and an RTO-capped prepaid offer.
